title: Capped empirical influential coordinates
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $t$ be a positive rational influence bound, and let $\varepsilon$ be a rational with $0<\varepsilon\le 1/2$. Form the uncapped empirical set using the prescribed samples; the empirical set is that set if its cardinality is at most the coordinate cap for $t,\varepsilon$, and is empty otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: samples are supplied for every singleton coordinate set and every index in the prescribed finite sample range
each sample is a pair of a length-$n$ sign vector and a sign
